name: FarmLinks at Pursell Farms
fine: Unofficial re-creation built from the mapped course layout (© OpenStreetMap contributors), USGS 3DEP elevation and published hole descriptions. Not affiliated with FarmLinks at Pursell Farms.
tips: “The Farm.” A 576-yard par 5 that bends gently right. Two bunkers pinch the landing area. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides.
“Sawmill.” A 416-yard par 4 that bends gently right. A bunker guards the green on the right. Water sits left of the green.
“Baby Rattler.” A 354-yard par 4 that plays straight away. A bunker guards the green on the right.

“Lower 40.” The hardest hole on the course climbs to a green perched on the hillside, with a stream crossing the fairway. A 472-yard par 4 that plays straight away. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides.
“Hang Time.” The signature hole: the tee sits on a hilltop near an old marble quarry, about 170 feet above the green. A 206-yard par 3. Three bunkers guard the green on both sides.

“Bootlegger.” Downhill off the tee, then back up to a perched green that falls away left and long. A 530-yard par 5 that bends gently left. Two bunkers pinch the landing area. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides.
“Big Daddy.” A 426-yard par 4 that plays straight away. Two bunkers pinch the landing area. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides.
“Back It Up.” Long but downhill and open; a miss short leaves a fair chip. A 250-yard par 3. A bunker guards the green on the left.
“Desoto.” A 451-yard par 4 that doglegs hard right. One bunker pinches the landing area. A bunker guards the green on the left. Water sits right of the green.

“Christine.” Lake Christine sits right of the tee shot; the fairway is wide. A 533-yard par 5 that doglegs hard right. Three bunkers pinch the landing area. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides. Water sits right of the hole.
“Lonely Pine.” A lone pine stands in the fairway; the best line is just left of it. A 428-yard par 4 that bends gently left. A bunker guards the green on the right.

“Eureka Railroad.” The old Eureka railroad bed runs through the right greenside bunker. A 467-yard par 4 that doglegs hard left. Two bunkers pinch the landing area. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides.
“Go For It.” Short and tempting: the risk-reward hole. A 369-yard par 4 that bends gently left. A bunker guards the green on the left.

“Swamp.” The flattest hole, with Pennywinkle Creek and the woods all down the left. A 434-yard par 4 that plays straight away. One bunker pinches the landing area. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides. Water sits right of the hole.
“Showcase.” A 223-yard par 3. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides.

“Dana's Pick.” Doglegs right and climbs to a perched, heavily contoured green. A 396-yard par 4 that bends gently right. One bunker pinches the landing area. Two bunkers guard the green on both sides.
“Big Gulp.” Over the pond to the green, with hardwoods behind. A 187-yard par 3. A bunker guards the green on the right. Water sits left of the green.

“Orchards.” A long, slightly uphill finish through the old orchard, with the Grille looking over the green. A 607-yard par 5 that plays straight away. One bunker pinches the landing area. A bunker guards the green on the left.
